paper_sections.title: Aging of visual word perception is related to decreased segregation within and beyond the word network in the brain
Data preprocessing for resting-state fMRI data
Between-group difference of behavioral performances in visual matching task
Between-group difference in resting-state functional connectivity

description.value: The study examined age-related differences in visual word perception using behavioral visual matching tasks, task-fMRI word localizer data, and resting-state seed-based functional connectivity of bilateral ventral occipitotemporal regions.

design.value: The study recruited healthy older and young adults, collected resting-state fMRI followed by task fMRI during a word localizer, and then assessed visual word and symbol-form matching behavior.

description.value: The standardized Chinese version was used for evaluating non-verbal intelligence quotient (IQ) and general cognitive ability.
Participants determined whether two visually presented words were identical and responded as quickly and accurately as possible; inverse efficiency score was calculated.
A baseline control test using symbol-form stimuli followed the same procedure as the word matching test.
The number of years of schooling was collected.

source_definition.value: between-subject variable age (older adults vs. young adults)
within-subject variable stimulus type (word pictures vs. symbol pictures)

description.value: 19 healthy older adults; all participants were right-handed individuals with no history of encephalopathy or mental illness.

medical_condition.value: healthy; no history of encephalopathy or mental illness

description.value: 22 young adults; all participants were right-handed individuals with no history of encephalopathy or mental illness. Data from three participants were missing for the behavioral tasks.

medical_condition.value: healthy; no history of encephalopathy or mental illness

task_description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were collected from all participants in a quiet state.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to rest adequately the day before the experiment and keep their heads as still as possible during the scan.

task_description.value: A block-designed localizer task presented Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters on the left or right side of fixation; participants judged stimulus location by pressing the corresponding button.

stimuli.value: Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters

instructions.value: Participants judged the location of the stimulus by pressing the corresponding button as accurately and quickly as possible.

task_performance_measures.value: location judgment accuracy and reaction time

task_description.value: Participants performed word matching and symbol-form matching tasks involving same/different judgments.

stimuli.value: 30 new pictures of words and 30 new pictures of symbols, all in stick figure style

instructions.value: Participants must quickly determine whether the two words on the screen are identical and press the corresponding button as swiftly and accurately as possible.

task_performance_measures.value: reaction time, proportion of correct responses, and inverse efficiency score (IES)

instrument.value: GE 3-Tesla MRI scanner (MR-750, GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI)

description.value: Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) was used to obtain rs-fMRI and task-fMRI data. The imaging parameters were 43 axial slices, flip angle 90°, field of view 220 × 220 mm2, and matrix size 64 × 64.

number_of_volumes.value: 240 contiguous volumes for resting-state; 245 time points in the continuous time course including the localizer

description.value: Task-fMRI data were preprocessed using the DPABI toolkit.

software.value: Data Processing and Analysis for Brain Imaging (DPABI), based on MATLAB

steps.value: removal of the first five time points
spatial normalization to the EPI template in MNI space
spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel with FWHM of 6 mm

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were preprocessed using the DPABI toolkit.

steps.value: removal of the first 10 time points
spatial normalization to the EPI template in MNI space
regression of Friston 24-parameter head motion profiles, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals

model_settings.value: The phase-scattered Chinese characters were used as a baseline; Chinese character images were contrasted against them to generate a linear contrast image for each participant.

estimator.value: one-sample t-test for the group-level activation map

model_settings.value: Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between averaged ROI time courses or between each ROI time course and every voxel time course, followed by Fisher’s r-to-z transformation.
2 × 2 repeated-measure ANOVA with age as the between-subject variable and stimulus type as the within-subject variable.
Partial correlations controlled for the IES from the symbol-form matching task and were calculated using the ppcor R package.

estimator.value: Pearson correlation coefficient and partial correlation

description.value: Participants rested in a quiet state during resting-state fMRI.
Visual stimulation consisting of Chinese character images.
Phase-scattered Chinese characters used as the baseline in the localizer task.
Word stimuli in the visual matching task.
Symbol-form stimuli used as a baseline control condition.

spatial_scope.value: one or more regions of interest

roi_definition.value: Based on the activation levels obtained in previous studies and the results from the localizer task in the present study, the left and right vOT regions were identified; the vOT consisted of areas in the Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) atlas.

lesser side of the Chinese characters vs. scattered Chinese characters contrast

definition.value: The linear contrast image Chinese characters vs. scattered Chinese characters was calculated to identify the brain regions sensitive to word perception for each participant, and the one-sample t-test was performed to obtain the older-adult group-level activation map; the most activated voxels within the left and right vOT were selected as seed voxels.

correction_scope.value: within the left and right vOT of each AAL region

interpretations.value: brain regions sensitive to word perception

spatial_unit.value: voxels and averaged ROI time courses

roi_definition.value: two spherical regions of interest with a radius of 5 mm centered on seed voxels selected from the group-level word localizer activation maps; the beyond-word-network analysis was performed within the AAL mask

roi_label.value: left ventral occipitotemporal area (lvOT) seed and the Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) mask

role.value: included in the between-group comparison; older adults showed increased FC

definition.value: A two-sample t-test compared the connectivity values of the lvOT seed with the right vOT and with other non-word-selective regions between older and young adult groups. Older adults exhibited increased FC between the lvOT and the right inferior temporal gyrus, right inferior parietal region, left inferior parietal region, left supplementary motor area, and right precuneus, as well as increased FC between the two word-selective ROIs.

specific_metric.value: Pearson correlation coefficients transformed into z-values via Fisher’s r-to-z transformation

inference_level.value: ROI connectivity values and voxels within the AAL mask

voxelwise_threshold_type.value: p-value: p < 0.001 at the voxel level for FC beyond the word network; p < 0.05 for the within-word-network ROI comparison

multiple_comparison_method.value: Gaussian Random Field (GRF) theory for multiple comparison correction beyond the word network

target_regions.value: right vOT, right inferior temporal gyrus (ITG.R), right inferior parietal region (IPL.R), left inferior parietal region (IPL.L), left supplementary motor area (SMA.L), and right precuneus (PCUN.R)

parameter_change.value: increased FC in older adults compared to young adults

model_representation_notes.value: Gender was included as a covariate in the beyond-word-network two-sample t-tests.

role.value: included in the between-group comparison; FC increased for some connections and decreased for others

definition.value: A two-sample t-test compared the connectivity values of the rvOT seed with other non-word-selective regions between older and young adult groups. Older adults exhibited increased FC between the rvOT and the right superior parietal gyrus (SPG.R) and right dorsolateral superior frontal gyrus (SFGdor.R), and decreased FC between the rvOT and the left lingual gyrus (LING.L) and left medial superior frontal gyrus (SFGmed.L).

parameter_change.value: increased FC in older adults between rvOT and SPG.R and SFGdor.R, and decreased FC in older adults between rvOT and LING.L and SFGmed.L

model_representation_notes.value: Gender was included as a covariate in the beyond-word-network two-sample t-tests.

interpretations.value: between-group differences in functional connectivity within and between the word network and other networks
